newsitem.title: USA: Brady debt mixed as market awaits U.S.jobs report.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt mixed as market awaits U.S.jobs report.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were mixed in thin trade late Thursday as market participants braced themselves for a more bearish scenario ahead of the U.S. employment report due out Friday, market experts said.

"I think the consensus is that it will be a bearish number and so I think people made their bets and aren't generally willing to stick their necks out as far as I can tell," said James Barrineau, emerging markets strategist at Smith Barney.
Trading sources noted though that floating rate bonds outperformed fixed-rate instruments as players positioned themselves for an ascending interest rate environment.

AT 1700 EST/2200 GMT Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR were 1/8 firmer at 89-1/4 bid whereas the country's par bonds AR4C23=RR were 3/8 lower at 64-5/8 bid. Mexican discounts MXFLL19=RR were 1/4 higher at 89-1/4 bid whereas its par bonds MX625L19=RR were 1/8 lower at 74 bid.

"We have been advising our clients for the past three or four days to completely forget about fixed rate (instruments) and focus on discounts and floating rate bonds. We are just advising investors to be defensive," said Richard Segal, chief economist at Santander Investments.
Market sources said that a bearish employment report Friday would certainly heighten speculation of a hike in U.S. interest rates at the next FOMC meeting on March 25.
"If it is a bearish number as expected people will just price in 25 basis points," said one source.

Barrineau said: "I think we are getting there in terms of pricing in 25 basis points so even if it's a bad number, I don't expect the sky to fall because I think we are halfway there to pricing it in."
In the broader market, sources said Venezuelan Bradys continued to rebound on the back of higher oil prices on the week and buying by a large fund.
"Oil is up almost one dollar from this week's lows so that is positive. There was also talk yesterday that one of the funds took an enormous position in Venezuela," said Segal.
Venezuelan DCBs VZFLL07=RR were 5/8 higher at 86-1/4 bid and its FLIRBS VZ6C97=RR were 1/2 better at 86-1/2 bid.

Elsewhere, Peru is expected to close it long-awaited Brady agreement with its commercial bank creditors Friday and sources said they expect some upward price movement in coming weeks despite the overall bearish outlook.
"If the market on the whole goes down, they (Peruvian debt) won't necessarily outperfrom but they should perform well over the next two to four weeks," said Segal.
Among Eastern European instruments, Bulgarian Bradys stayed higher late in the day on hopes that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) will lend support.

"The assumption of the market is that if Bulgaria makes it through 1997 than everything will be fine. Any event or hint which clarifies the picture for 1997 is being latched on with a lot of vigor," said market expert.
Bulgarian IABs BGFLTH11=RR were two percentage points higher at 59-1/2 bid.
In other news, market experts said a positive reception to Russian President Boris Yeltsin's state of the union address earlier today helped to bolster prices.
Russian Vnesheconombank dollar loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were one percentage point higher at 81 bid.
